# YouTube Transcript with Timestamps (Free)

Get a YouTube transcript with clickable timestamps. Copy it, download as TXT or SRT, or jump to any moment. Free, no login.

To get a YouTube transcript with timestamps, paste the video URL into YTTranscript and keep timestamps on — you'll get the full text with a time marker on every line, free.

Timestamps turn a YouTube transcript from a block of text into a navigable document. With timestamps, you can jump directly to any moment in a video, cite a specific quote with precision, or create chapter links for your own content. This guide explains how to get a YouTube transcript with timestamps and how to use them effectively.

## How to Get a YouTube Transcript with Timestamps

### Method 1: YTTranscript (Recommended)

YTTranscript gives you a full transcript with timestamps included by default.

  1. Copy the YouTube video URL
  2. Go to yttranscript.app
  3. Paste the URL and click Get Transcript Now
  4. The transcript appears with timestamps on the left of each segment

You can then choose to download with or without timestamps — the toggle is available before you download. All three formats (TXT, DOCX, PDF) support timestamp inclusion.

### Method 2: YouTube's Built-in Transcript Viewer

On desktop, click the three-dot menu below the video and select "Show transcript". Timestamps appear by default on the left of each line. You can toggle them off using the menu inside the transcript panel. There's no download button — you must manually copy the text.

# YouTube Transcript with Timestamps: Copy and Download Every Line with Its Time

Get a YouTube transcript with a timestamp on every line, then copy it or download it with the timings intact. One toggle hides them when you just want text.

YouTube video URL [Input: Paste a YouTube URL here…] Get Free Transcript

  * A time on every line
  * Click a line to seek
  * TXT, SRT, VTT, Markdown

This tool gives you a YouTube transcript with timestamps for any video that has captions. Paste a link, press Get Free Transcript and switch on the Timestamps toggle: every caption line now starts with the moment it is spoken, such as 2:05 or 1:02:03. Click any line and the embedded video jumps straight to that point, which makes it easy to check a quote before you use it.

You can copy the YouTube transcript with timestamps in one click, or download it with the timings kept as a TXT file, an SRT or VTT subtitle file, Markdown with clickable time links, Word or PDF. It is a free YouTube transcript with timestamps tool that runs in the browser, so you can get a YouTube transcript with timestamps on a computer or a phone without installing anything or creating an account.

Because the timings come straight from YouTube's caption track, they match the captions you see when you press CC in the player. Nothing is re-timed or estimated on our side.

### A worked example

A 10 minute 31 second talk-heavy video with an English auto-generated track has 666 caption lines and about 6,400 words, and it loads here in roughly one to two seconds the first time. One of its cues starts at 125,400 ms. In the transcript with timestamps on, that line reads 2:05 followed by its words. In the SRT download the same cue starts at 00:02:05,400, and in the VTT download at 00:02:05.400. Click the line and the video seeks to 2:05. With timestamps on, Copy transcript puts all 666 lines on your clipboard, each with its own time.

## How to get a YouTube transcript with timestamps

It takes about a minute to get a YouTube transcript with timestamps, on desktop or mobile.

  1. ### 1. Copy the video link

Copy the address from your browser, or tap Share and Copy link in the YouTube app. Watch, youtu.be, Shorts, live and embed links all work.

  2. ### 2. Paste it and load the transcript

Paste the link into the box above and press Get Free Transcript. The transcript appears next to the video.

  3. ### 3. Switch the Timestamps toggle on

Timestamps are hidden by default. Turn the toggle on and every line starts with its time, such as 3:42.

  4. ### 4. Copy or download with timings

Press Copy transcript to copy every line with its time, or choose TXT, SRT, VTT, Markdown, Word or PDF to download the transcript with timestamps.

## Timestamps on translated transcripts

When you translate the transcript into one of 106 languages, it is translated line by line and every line keeps its original timestamp. Click-to-seek still works, and an SRT or VTT downloaded from the translated view keeps the source timings, which gives you a timed subtitle draft in another language. The translation is machine translation, so check it before publishing.

## How accurate are YouTube transcript timestamps?

The timestamps are the timings in YouTube's caption track, so they are as accurate as the captions in the player. Creator-uploaded subtitles are usually timed carefully. Automatic captions are timed by YouTube's speech recognition and are normally close, though a line can start slightly before or after the word you hear, and the words themselves can be wrong with music, accents or names.

If a video has no captions there are no timestamps to show, and private, age-restricted and members-only videos fail because they need a signed-in session that we do not use or bypass.

## Frequently asked questions

How do I get a YouTube transcript with timestamps?

Paste the video link above, press Get Free Transcript and switch the Timestamps toggle on. Every line then starts with its time.

How do I download a YouTube transcript with timestamps?

Turn timestamps on and download TXT for timed plain text, or download SRT or VTT for subtitle files with start and end times.

Can I copy a YouTube transcript with timestamps?

Yes. With the toggle on, Copy transcript copies one line per caption, each starting with its time.

Is this YouTube transcript with timestamps tool free?

Yes. It is free, with no sign-up and no extension.

Are the timestamps accurate?

They are the timings in YouTube's caption track, so they match the captions you see in the player.

Can I remove the timestamps?

Switch the toggle off. Copy and TXT then give you clean text. SRT and VTT always keep timings.

Can I turn the timestamps into YouTube chapters?

The summary page drafts chapter timestamps starting at 0:00 that you can paste into your description and edit.

How do I share a link to one timestamp?

Use the timestamp link tool. Enter the video URL and a time such as 1:23 to get a youtu.be link that starts there.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Questions

How do I get the transcript of a YouTube video?
    Paste the video's link above and press Get transcript. You get every word with timestamps, which you can copy or download as a text file. YouTube also has its own transcript (open the description and choose Show transcript), but only on videos with captions, and automatic captions come without punctuation or speakers.

Is it free?
    If anyone has transcribed the same video in the last 30 days, yes: you get it instantly with a free account. A new transcript needs Pro, shared with the Claude connector: 20 hours of video a month, 7 days free, then $60 a year, or $8 a month. A 10-minute video uses 10 minutes.

Why do I need to sign in?
    The transcript is written by Google's Gemini model, which costs money for every minute of video and may only be offered to adults. An account lets us keep the service for people aged 18 and over and count your minutes. Signing in with Google takes one click.

Does it work on videos without captions?
    Yes. It listens to the audio rather than copying YouTube's captions, so it works on videos that have no captions at all.

How accurate is it?
    On our test videos (a commencement speech, a phone review and a Turkish talk), the transcript differed from YouTube's own captions on 2 to 5 words in 100, and timestamps were within about 10 seconds. Song lyrics over loud music are much less reliable.

Which languages does it support?
    It writes the transcript in the language that is spoken. To get it in another language, ask Claude to translate it.

Which videos work?
    Public YouTube videos, including Shorts and past live streams, up to three hours. Private and unlisted videos don't work. If your minutes run out partway through a video, you get the transcript up to that point.

Do you keep the video or the transcript?
    We never download the video: Google's model reads the public YouTube link directly. Transcripts of public videos are kept for 30 days so the next person who asks gets them instantly; they contain nothing about who asked.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## What creators do with a YouTube transcript

  * Study why a video worked: read the first 30 seconds of a top video in your niche on one screen and see exactly how the hook and the promise are built.
  * Turn a video into posts: use the transcript as the source for a LinkedIn post, an X thread, a newsletter or a carousel instead of starting from a blank page.
  * Quote accurately: pull exact lines for show notes, articles or research, with the timestamp to link back to the moment.
  * Write captions and chapters: use the timestamped version to draft chapters, descriptions and on-screen captions faster.
  * Search your own back catalogue: keep transcripts of your videos in one document so you can find what you said, and when, without rewatching.

## Why use this instead of YouTube’s own transcript panel?

YouTube can show a transcript under many videos, but it is built for following along, not for reusing the text. It comes as short caption fragments with a timestamp on every line, and copying it cleanly takes several steps.

  * One click to copy the whole transcript, without the timestamps getting in the way.
  * Sentences are joined into readable paragraphs instead of 3-second caption fragments.
  * Download as a .txt file, and it works the same on your phone.
  * Works the same for YouTube Shorts and live replays as for regular videos.
